harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured persistent, system-wide sudo command auditing on node1. Commands are timestamped with the invoking user in /var/log/sudo-commands.log and excluded from general logs. Configuration and audit data survived the mandatory node reboot.
actions_performed: Added /etc/sudoers.d/99-sudo-command-logging with root ownership and mode 0440.
Configured sudo to write to /var/log/sudo-commands.log and disabled sudo command syslog output.
Validated the complete sudoers configuration with visudo.
Verified command attribution, timestamps, and zero marker occurrences in auth.log and syslog.
Restarted node1 safely and confirmed a changed boot identity.
Confirmed Ubuntu 16.04 and kernel 4.4.0-210-generic remained unchanged after restart.
Verified rsyslog, sudo policy, historical audit data, and new sudo logging after restart.

evidence.requirement: Record every sudo command with the invoking user and timestamp in /var/log/sudo-commands.log
evidence.summary: The globally applied sudoers policy parsed successfully; captured entries show timestamps, invoking user antrieb, run-as user root, working directory, and executed commands.

evidence.requirement: Keep sudo command entries out of the general system log
evidence.summary: Unique pre- and post-restart command markers were recorded in the dedicated log, with zero occurrences in auth.log or syslog.

evidence.requirement: Preserve the installed operating-system release and kernel

evidence.summary: Healthy baseline used boot ID 0256e3f5-9f2d-48f3-b55b-12f9f4d599ab; restart was acknowledged; post-restart boot ID changed to bdf68084-6561-41cf-9467-2294e3db62e9; rsyslog, valid sudo policy, prior audit data, and new isolated logging all recovered.
